sandbox.activate_tmpl:
# workwood sandbox — source this file:   source %[1]s/activate
# Activates an ISOLATED workwood (its own home + the bundled binary on PATH).
# Nothing here touches your real ~/.workwood.
_WW_SBX="%[1]s"
export WORKWOOD_HOME="$_WW_SBX/home"
case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$_WW_SBX/bin:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$_WW_SBX/bin:$PATH" ;;
esac
echo "workwood sandbox active  (WORKWOOD_HOME=$WORKWOOD_HOME)"
echo "project 'sandbox' is registered and default."
echo "try:  workwood sf list  ·  workwood compose helloworld welcome  ·  workwood"
sandbox.walkthrough_tmpl:
# workwood sandbox

A throwaway, fully self-contained playground for the `workwood` CLI. Everything
lives under this directory — an isolated home, sample repos with their own local
git "origins", a team super-repo, and a copy of the `workwood` binary. None of
it touches your real ~/.workwood or GitHub. Delete this folder to clean up.

## Start

```sh
source %[1]s/activate
```

That sets `WORKWOOD_HOME` to this sandbox and puts the bundled `workwood` on your
PATH. The project `sandbox` is already registered and default.

## What's here

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `home/` | the isolated `WORKWOOD_HOME` (registry, seeded plugins, your target state) |
| `super/` | the super-repo: `workwood.yaml`, `super-features/`, a project-local `plugins/context` |
| `main/` | base clones (`api`, `web`, `worker`) — pre-populated; each has a `.workwood/` folder |
| `origins/` | bare git repos acting as each sample repo's `origin` |
| `features/` | where your feature worktrees get checked out |
| `bin/` | a copy of the `workwood` binary |

## Try it — the plugin model

```sh
workwood sf list                      # one shared sample feature: welcome
workwood compose helloworld welcome   # PARENT 'hello ' + each repo's CHILD 'world'
workwood compose context welcome      # a project-local plugin: dump the resolved context

# create your own feature spanning repos
workwood sf create play "my playground"
workwood sf add play api feature/login    # branch play/feature/login
workwood sf add play web ui
workwood sf add play worker jobs
workwood compose helloworld play      # -> "hello world" once per repo
```

## Targets are additive (per repo, multiple setups)

```sh
workwood sf target list play                 # each repo's setups (auto by default)
workwood sf target add play api worktree     # source api from its worktree
workwood sf target add play api deploy        # ALSO add a custom 'deploy' setup (additive!)
workwood compose context play                # api now shows up TWICE — worktree + deploy

workwood sf target add play --all main       # bulk: add 'main' to every repo in the feature
workwood sf target add play web ignore        # drop web from composition
workwood sf target remove play api deploy     # remove one setup
workwood sf target clear play api             # reset api to auto
```

Built-in targets are `ignore` · `main` · `worktree`. Anything else (like
`deploy`) is a CUSTOM target — workwood just passes the string to that repo's
`.workwood` child, which decides what it means.

## Scaffolding children with --init

A plugin can scaffold its child into each repo's `.workwood/` folder:

```sh
workwood compose helloworld play --init   # writes .workwood/helloworld into each repo
workwood compose tmux       play --init   # writes a starter .workwood/tmux
workwood compose tmux       play          # one tmux window per repo (needs tmux)
workwood compose ssh        play          # jump into a repo's .workwood/ssh
```

The sample repos already ship `.workwood/{up,ssh,helloworld}`, so the demos work
without --init.

## The TUI

```sh
workwood                              # interactive editor for the selected project
```

`t` adds a target setup to the highlighted repo · `T` adds one to many repos at
once · `c` clears a repo back to auto.

## Notes

- Sample repos are real git repos with real local origins, so `git push` inside a
  worktree works (it pushes to `origins/`). `repos pull` fetches from there too.
- `compose context` is a project-local plugin (in `super/plugins/`) — proof a
  team can ship plugins with its manifests. `helloworld`/`tmux`/`ssh` are the
  global defaults seeded into `home/plugins/`.
- Done playing? Just `rm -rf` this directory.

usage.main:
workwood — git-worktree orchestration for multi-repo super-features

Usage:
  workwood                                 launch the interactive super-feature editor (TUI)
  workwood sandbox [path]                  scaffold a self-contained playground to try the tool
  workwood init [path]                     register a super-repo + where you keep its checkouts
  workwood project <list|use|remove>       manage the project registry (~/.workwood/config.yaml)
  workwood repos  [pull|list]              manage base reference clones in the project's main_dir
  workwood super-feature <subcommand>      manage a super-feature (alias: sf; see: workwood sf help)
  workwood compose <plugin> <feature> [--init]  run a plugin (e.g. tmux, ssh); --init scaffolds its .workwood children
  workwood plugins                         list available plugins
  workwood lang [en|ja]                    show or set the UI language
  workwood version                         print the build + file-schema version

Global:
  -p, --project <name>                     act on a specific project (else: cwd-detected, then default)
usage.feature:
Usage: workwood super-feature <command> [args]   (alias: sf)

Commands:
  create <name> [description]                     create a super-feature manifest
  add    <name> <repo> <worktree-branch-name> [--from <source>] [--no-feature-prefix]
                                                  add a worktree (from <repo>) on branch <name>/<worktree-branch-name>
  up     <name>                                   rebuild all worktrees from the manifest
  target add    <name> [<repo>|--all|--repo r …] <ignore|main|worktree|custom> [worktree-path]
                                                  add a setup to repos' additive target lists
  target remove <name> <repo> <setup> [worktree-path]   drop one setup
  target clear  <name> <repo>                     reset a repo to the automatic default
  target list   <name>                            show each repo's setups
  remove <name> <repo> [sub-branch] [--prune-branch]
                                                  remove ONE worktree (+ optionally its branch)
  down   <name>                                   remove ALL worktrees, keep the manifest
  status <name>                                   branch + dirty state per worktree
  list                                            list all super-features
  delete <name> [--prune-branches]                remove worktrees + manifest (+ branches)
